payload_json.case_name: Sham Wing Kan v Commissioner of Police
payload_json.exact_quote: Section 50(6) on a proper construction authorizes police officers to search the digital contents of a mobile phone
payload_json.proposition_text: The Court of Appeal declared that section 50(6) PFO authorizes warrantless search of a seized mobile phone's digital contents only in exigent circumstances.

payload_json.case_name: Sham Wing Kan v Commissioner of Police
payload_json.exact_quote: a search of the digital contents of a mobile phone (as opposed to the mobile phone itself as an object) as a specie of the power of search by law enforcement officer incidental to arrest is governed by the common law instead of Section 50
payload_json.proposition_text: The Court of Appeal held that search of digital contents on a phone seized on arrest is governed by the common law power of search incidental to arrest rather than section 50(6) PFO.

payload_json.case_name: Sham Wing Kan v Commissioner of Police
payload_json.exact_quote: any warrantless search must be subject to scrutiny under the proportionality test
payload_json.proposition_text: The Court of Appeal held that any warrantless search of digital phone contents must satisfy the proportionality test.

payload_json.case_name: Sham Wing Kan v Commissioner of Police
payload_json.exact_quote: the general considerations discussed therein on the importance of safeguards by way of prior judicial scrutiny apply equally to a search of the digital contents of a mobile phone
payload_json.proposition_text: The Court of Appeal applied Keen Lloyd safeguards, emphasizing prior judicial scrutiny for intrusive warrantless digital searches.

payload_json.case_name: Lai Chee Ying v Commissioner of Police
payload_json.proposition_text: The Court of Appeal held that 'specified evidence' under NSL Implementation Rules Schedule 1 covers journalistic material.

payload_json.case_name: Lai Chee Ying v Commissioner of Police
payload_json.exact_quote: the protection afforded to journalistic material is not absolute
payload_json.proposition_text: The Court of Appeal held that protection for journalistic material in search cases is important but not absolute.

payload_json.case_name: Lai Chee Ying v Commissioner of Police
payload_json.exact_quote: it would unduly limit the scope and hence reduce the effectiveness of police investigation
payload_json.proposition_text: The Court of Appeal reasoned that excluding journalistic material from 'specified evidence' would unduly limit effective police investigation in NSL cases.
